newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Unocal unit says no pact yet on workers.
newsitem.headline: Unocal unit says no pact yet on workers.

text.p: Philippine Geothermal Inc (PGI), a subsidiary of Unocal Corp, said on Tuesday a Department of Labour and Employment (DOLE) return-to-work order for labour union members who staged a strike did not cover the reinstatement of employees who were part of the company's downsizing programme.

"We have not agreed to reinstate any of the 168 employees they said were dismissed. These employees were not dismissed... but they were covered by the company's rightsizing (downsizing) programme," said Edgar Sevilla, PGI spokesman.
In a statement last Monday, the PGI Employees Union said that it ended a strike "after PGI agreed to reinstate 168 dismissed employees and stop further layoffs."
PGI was undertaking a corporate downsizing when its workers staged a strike at the National Power Corp's 426-megawatt MakBan geothermal plant and 330-mw Tiwi plant in northern Philippines.
PGI is the developer of the MakBan and Tiwi geothermal steam fields. The power plants supply about 17 percent of the power requirements of the main island of Luzon.
On January 10, DOLE issued an order assuming jurisdiction over the strike and ordering strikers to return to work.
The order required the company to accept striking workers under the same terms and conditions of employment as before the strike.

The department order also requires management and the union to resolve within 20 days disputed issues including demands for the reinstatement of employees who were part of the company's downsizing programme.
